subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The American Federation of Teachers (AFT) was founded in 1916 by representatives of eight local teacher unions.
• The AFT was created to improve working conditions and educational standards for teachers.
• Charles Stillman was the AFT's first president.
• In 1965, the US Department of Labor recognized teachers' right to collective bargaining in federal legislation.
• This legislation formally established teachers' rights to negotiate contracts and working conditions.
• The lobbying efforts of the AFT were instrumental in securing this recognition.
prompt: The student wants to identify an accomplishment of the AFT. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The AFT's lobbying efforts were instrumental in securing federal recognition of teachers' right to collective bargaining in 1965.
choices.B: The AFT, founded by representatives of eight local teacher unions, had Charles Stillman as its first president.
choices.C: Founded in 1916, the AFT was created by representatives of local unions to improve working conditions for teachers.
choices.D: In 1965, the AFT established teachers' rights to negotiate contracts, legislation that improved working conditions for teachers.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence directly identifies an accomplishment of the AFT: that its lobbying efforts were instrumental in securing federal recognition of teachers' right to collective bargaining.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The sentence misrepresents the information in the notes: the US Department of Labor, not the AFT, established the federal recognition of teachers' rights.
